text:
Maria L.: FYI — product is proposing a "Pro Plus" packaging tweak that raises per-minute token windows for paid tiers. PM expects a regional skew toward EU by ~30% for short interactive calls. Need a quick probabilistic capacity forecast (3 weeks) and suggested mitigation (pre-warm / reserved pool). Can infra run a sim today? :eyes:

Ashwin P.: On it. Quick Q: is PM assuming sustained or bursty traffic? window bump usually causes spikes not steady-state.

Maria L.: Mostly bursty. Think more short chats (2–8s) but higher QPS for those minutes. They expect more European traffic because feature hits EU partners first.

Julie H.: I'll pull last 8 weeks of session length + per-region QPS. If bursts are 2–8s, batching effectiveness drops. That changes GPU-hour per 1k tokens.

Ryan (oncall): Add networking constraint: eu-west AZ-B had higher packet loss during last sprint — if we put more reserved capacity there we should prefer eu-west-2 vs eu-west-1. Also watch regional EBS limits for pre-warm nodes.

Samir K.: Doing a quick back-of-envelope. Baseline: 12k GPU-hours/week total across regions. If EU gets +30% of sessions but sessions are 40% shorter, net EU GPU-hours \u2248 +18% and global +6% assuming no change to US load. Burstiness increases headroom requirement due to reduced batching.

Ashwin P.: I ran a low-sample sim (100 draws) with the current latency SLO target (p95 < 120ms). Results: 95th percentile concurrent model replicas needed in EU goes from 24 -> 36 for burst scenario. That implies ~480 -> 720 GPU-hours/day regionally.

Samir K.: Quick cost delta estimate: average spot A100 cost we use ~ $3.8/hr. Extra EU GPU-hours/day ~240 => ~$912/day -> ~$27k/month. If we use reserved/dedicated it's cheaper per-hour but requires commitment.

Julie H.: Pasting the minimal sim config I used (small):
```
scenario: pro_plus_eu_burst
horizon_days: 21
samples: 1000
session_len_dist: mixture(exp(2s), exp(6s))
qps_shift: {eu: 0.30, us: -0.05}
batching_eff: -35%
```

Ashwin P.: Action items I propose:
- Run full sim (1k samples) and produce per-region GPU-hour CDF + cost curve.
- Temp bump autoscaler max replicas in eu-west-2 and add a fast-burst pool (40 GPUs) for 3 weeks.
- Exec decision on reserved vs spot for that pool by EOD (finance).
- Update routing policy to fall back to us-west-1 at 95th percentile load.

Ryan (oncall): For the pre-warm pool, coordinate with eng-infra to avoid hitting quota limits. I can open a support ticket for temporary EBS/eni increases in eu-west-2 and tag nodes as "pro-plus-burst-2026".

Maria L.: Thanks. PM asked for a single-slide summary for leadership by EOD with: 3-week worst-case GPU-hours, cost delta, and recommended mitigation. Can we have that? :pray:

Samir K.: I'll produce the slide after the 1k-sample run. Early numbers (p90) for 3-week horizon: +3.6k GPU-hours EU total -> ~$13.7k; global +1.2k -> ~$4.6k. If we reserve 40 GPUs for 21 days (dedicated), rough committed cost $3.0/hr * 40 * 21 * 24 = ~$60.5k — so reserved is only worth it if traffic stays high after trial.

capacity-bot: Reminder: quota check passed for eu-west-2 but ephemeral IPs at 72% used. Recommend freeing unused ELBs or file a quota increase ticket.

Ashwin P.: I'll start the 1k-run now: `./forecast.py --scenario pro_plus_eu_burst --horizon 21 --samples 1000 --out proplus_eu_1k.json`

Julie H.: I'll assemble the slide deck skeleton with paste-in charts. Expect first draft in ~3 hours.

Maria L.: Perfect. If anyone spots a large mismatch vs Samir's early numbers, ping me. Otherwise we'll prep the canary and finance ask. :thumbsup:
